title: 422 Global Sumud Flotilla Activists Arrive in Turkey After Israeli Deportation; Accounts of Abuse Emerge
detail: On Day 954 of the Gaza war (May 22, 2026), 422 Global Sumud Flotilla activists arrived in Turkey after Israel deported them in the wake of the May 21 mass deportation operation. Turkey chartered three planes and flew the activists — including 85 Turkish nationals — from southern Israel. Activists reported being subjected to rubber bullets, punching, handcuffing, kicking, and being transported in leg chains to Ben Gurion Airport. An Italian journalist confirmed being beaten. The arrivals prompted Turkey to recall its ambassador from Tel Aviv and triggered a wave of formal diplomatic protests: Italy demanded an EU-level discussion on sanctions against National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir; Greece, Germany, France, Canada, Spain, the UK, and the Netherlands summoned Israeli ambassadors. The diplomatic fallout over Ben-Gvir's taunting video of bound and kneeling detainees continued to intensify. The 58-vessel Global Sumud Flotilla had departed from multiple European ports in April 2026 carrying humanitarian aid bound for Gaza, where a catastrophic aid shortfall persists — only ~110 trucks/day entering versus 600+ required.

title: Netanyahu Publicly Distances from Ben-Gvir's Flotilla Video; Italy Pushes EU Sanctions as Diplomatic Crisis Deepens
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly stated on May 22, 2026 (Day 954) that National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's conduct in posting footage of bound and kneeling flotilla detainees at Ashdod Port was 'not in line with Israel's values and norms.' Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar echoed the rebuke, calling it a 'disgraceful display.' The Times of Israel editorial board published a piece calling on Netanyahu to fire Ben-Gvir but noting he almost certainly would not. Italy's government formally called on the European Union to open discussions on targeted sanctions against Ben-Gvir. Ben-Gvir — who runs the Otzma Yehudit party and chairs the National Security Ministry controlling Israeli police — has faced previous calls for dismissal but remains a key coalition partner. The diplomatic fallout extends beyond the Ben-Gvir video: 10 foreign ministers had jointly condemned flotilla raids as 'blatant violations of international law'; UN human rights experts called for an independent investigation; comparisons to the 2010 Mavi Marmara incident proliferated across European media. The Saudi media outlet Asharq Al-Awsat also reported it had obtained what it described as a near-final draft of a US-Iran nuclear deal — a development tracked in parallel by Israeli intelligence and noted in Israeli media as bearing potential implications for regional security dynamics.

title: IDF Strikes Continue Across Central and Southern Gaza on Day 954; Cumulative Death Toll Surpasses 73,800
detail: Israeli Defense Forces continued near-daily airstrike operations across central and southern Gaza Strip on May 22, 2026 (Day 954 of the conflict, Day 12 of the renewed military campaign following the May 10 security cabinet authorization). Strikes targeted residual Hamas tunnel infrastructure and weapons caches in central Gaza and the Yellow Line buffer zone in the south. The cumulative Palestinian death toll since October 7, 2023 has surpassed 73,800 confirmed killed (Gaza Ministry of Health), with 172,600+ wounded. The OCHA Situation Report data indicates 856 Palestinians were killed and 2,463 wounded during the 212-day ceasefire window (October 10, 2025–May 10, 2026) and further deaths have accumulated since resumed operations on May 11. The UN reports that 94% of Gaza's hospitals are damaged or destroyed; 51% of essential medicines are at zero stock; and the 2026 UN Humanitarian Flash Appeal ($4.1B required) remains only 9.7% funded. IDF Chief of Staff Gen. Eyal Zamir stated that the renewed campaign will continue until Hamas demilitarizes or is destroyed. Since the October 2025 ceasefire broke down, IDF has conducted operations in eastern Rafah, the Yellow Line, Khan Younis, Al-Maghazi, and eastern Gaza City — with ACLED documenting a 35% increase in Israeli attacks since April 2026.
